original_question: Let Γ be a graph of diameter d. For i ∈ {1, 2,..., d}, let Γi be the graph on the same vertex set as Γ with vertices u, w adjacent in Γi if and only if dΓ (u, w) = i. Does there exist a Q-polynomial distance-regular graph Γ of diameter 3 such that Γ2 and Γ3 are strongly regular? A. A. Makhnëv
target_in_paper: Problem 21.90 in the section New Problems (21st issue, 2026): the existence of a Q-polynomial distance-regular graph of diameter 3 whose distance-2 and distance-3 graphs are strongly regular.
correct_elements: Your draft already reproduces the paper’s problem essentially verbatim: it defines the distance-i graph Γ_i using the graph distance d_Γ(u,w), restricts to diameter 3, and asks exactly whether there exists a Q-polynomial distance-regular graph Γ such that Γ_2 and Γ_3 are strongly regular.
refined_question: Let Γ be a graph of diameter d, and for each i ∈ {1,2,…,d} let Γ_i be the graph on the same vertex set as Γ in which two vertices u,w are adjacent if and only if d_Γ(u,w)=i. Does there exist a Q-polynomial distance-regular graph Γ of diameter 3 such that both Γ_2 and Γ_3 are strongly regular?
justification: The draft is already the exact open problem stated in the paper. The notation for the distance graphs Γ_i is introduced immediately before the question itself, and the paper does not give a narrower reformulation, an equivalent criterion, or additional hidden hypotheses nearby. So the faithful refinement is simply a cleaned-up stand-alone restatement of Problem 21.90.
